findings.evidence: The fix report's own account (waveS-lane06-fix.md, 'SPEC-1141-AC1'): the ticket's own instrument (PRE-FIX B4 cell, ten runs beside a parallel whole unit-suite run) was run and did NOT reproduce (10 green / 0 red of 10, both pre-fix and post-fix). No orchestrator/owner waiver is recorded in this worktree in its place, which is what the original finding's required_fix asked for absent a reproduction. What was substituted — an in-page activeElement sampler showing the trace ["BUTTON","BODY","H2"] across four independent runs — is real, useful diagnostic evidence of the mechanism, and is honestly distinguished in both the fix report and apps/web/e2e/README.md from a reproduced red. It does not satisfy AC1's literal text. This recheck did not attempt its own reproduction runs (the ticket's own instrument already consumed a bounded budget without success, and repeating it here would not change the outcome without a materially different load shape).
findings.disposition: Carry forward for the orchestrator: either accept the mechanism evidence (sampler trace + the pre-existing vacuity control that reds the polled cell when restoreFocusAfterRow's landmark.focus() is dropped) as sufficient in AC1's place with an explicit ruling, or leave #1141 open against this one acceptance criterion. AC2 (whole browser suite green twice, no B4 red) IS met — three full 589-passed runs are recorded, including one with the pre-fix cell in place — so this is a partial, not a wholesale, gap.

findings.title: #1044 AC3 (the db-live-gates driver green five consecutive times on a fresh database) remains unmet as a whole-driver run
findings.evidence: The fix report's own gate table: leg 1 (intake-e2e) 5/5 green; leg 2 (intake-admission-e2e) 0/5 — its terminal waitForQueueDrain cannot complete on any database carrying real client data, diagnosed concretely (held wake tasks minted from the cloned estate's own compliance/lint notifications while both clara.wake_engine_sources rows are disabled — a rig/estate property, not a #1044 code path); leg 3 (intake-batch-e2e) 4/5 green, one round-2 red at intake-batch-e2e.mjs:650 under load, also diagnosed concretely (a child settling between the cancel decision and the belt sweep, an allowance the cell already makes for the seed-to-decision window but not for the decision-to-belt window). No round in this lane ever ran the DRIVER (all three legs as db-live-gates actually runs them) green once, let alone five consecutive times — the AC's own wording. Lint (exit 0, independently reconfirmed by this recheck) and the WSL runtime-file run (independently reconfirmed: intake-sidecar-race 22/22, l9-pool-contract-lane-probe 28/28, though this recheck ran them on the Windows host rather than under WSL as user runner — the fix report's own WSL run is not re-verified here) are the two other AC3 clauses, both satisfied.
findings.disposition: Both gaps are diagnosed as properties of the rig (a used clara_l08-derived clone vs CI's from-scratch clara_intake_ci) and of a pre-existing cell (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:650, filed as a follow-up, not caused by this lane's change), not as defects in #1044's own fix — ADV-L06-01's lock and its non-vacuity were independently reproduced by this recheck (see findings_confirmed_fixed) and are sound. Per the original finding's own required_fix, closing AC3 needs the integrator to run the real driver on a genuinely fresh database (matching CI's clara_intake_ci shape) — something this lane's worktree, bound to a rig-cloned lane cluster, cannot produce. Carry forward to the integrator/release evidence rather than back to this lane.
